# Internet Archive Wayback Machine

> > A digital library preserving billions of web pages, software, books, audio, images, and videos for universal access to knowledge.

The Internet Archive, founded in 1996, operates the Wayback Machine—the world's largest web archive containing over 866 billion saved pages. It also hosts collections from institutions like NASA, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, Librivox, and preserves digital artifacts including MS-DOS software, Grateful Dead recordings, and historical datasets from USGS.

## Key Topics

- Wayback Machine
- Internet Archive
- Web archiving and preservation
- Digital library collections
- Software preservation (MS-DOS)
- Audio archives (Librivox, Grateful Dead)
- Image collections (Flickr Commons, Metropolitan Museum)
- Historical web snapshots
- NASA and USGS datasets
- Community-contributed content
- Universal access to knowledge
- Cultural heritage preservation
- Search engines history
- Alexa Internet crawl data

## Core Services

- [Wayback Machine](http://web.archive.org): Internet Archive homepage featuring Wayback Machine and digital collections
- [Wayback Machine (HTTPS)](https://web.archive.org): Internet Archive homepage with Wayback Machine web archive access

- [MSN Search (December 2000)](https://web.archive.org/all/20001205055600/http:/www.search.msn.com): Archived MSN Search engine homepage from December 2000
